scientific_question: When local small-mammal abundance rises, is crowding accommodated primarily by contraction of individual space use, expansion of the population footprint, or a cross-scale combination of both?

already_established: individual home-range size commonly decreases with density
NEON Peromyscus home-range area decreases with density
habitat, latitude and density interact to influence Peromyscus home-range area
within- versus between-individual variation in space use is an established conceptual decomposition
literature_boundary.candidate_contribution: jointly estimate abundance responses at individual and population spatial scales within the same standardized small-mammal sampling sessions
literature_boundary.key_reference: O'Fallon S, Pinter-Wollman N, Mabry KE. 2025. Oecologia 207:98. doi:10.1007/s00442-025-05731-2

future_confirmation.response: first NEON small-mammal observations not contained in RELEASE-2026

primary_unit: species x plotID x sampling session/eventID

sampling_boundary.primary_cross_scale_pool: multi-night sessions where both individual-scale and population-footprint metrics are estimable
sampling_boundary.one_night_sessions: population-footprint development only unless a future frozen model establishes comparability

candidate_individual_scale_metrics: within-individual squared radial spread around session centroid
session-level SCR/SECR spatial scale where estimable
candidate_population_footprint_metrics: effort-conditioned mean pairwise distance among individual session centres
effort-conditioned variance of individual session centres
effective occupied-trap number standardized by an effort/N-preserving null
mechanical_rejection_rule: reject any footprint metric that is a deterministic or near-deterministic function of abundance, occupied-trap count, nominal grid size, or grid identity

primary_hypothesis.name: cross_scale_density_accommodation
primary_hypothesis.individual_slope: beta_W = abundance response of individual-scale spatial extent
primary_hypothesis.population_slope: beta_B = abundance response of population-footprint spatial extent
primary_hypothesis.interpretation: additional individuals are accommodated more by spatial packing/compression at the individual scale than by proportional expansion of the population footprint

abundance_candidates: resolved unique individuals / MNKA-like session count
closed or spatial capture-recapture density where estimable
required_controls: audit repeated-location support versus session abundance
fixed-footprint mechanical null across varying sampled individual count
same prospectively defined individual-support rule for primary W/B comparison

replication_requirement.exact_minimums: freeze after effect-blind RELEASE-2026 structural audit and copy unchanged to future-response contract

stop_rules: stop if both spatial scales are not jointly estimable across replicated species and sites
stop if footprint metric is mechanically driven by abundance
stop if within-individual metric is dominated by sparse recapture support
stop if effort or taxonomy semantics cannot be frozen prospectively
do not rescue future failure with post-hoc taxa, thresholds, metrics, habitat moderators, or incompatible sampling designs

individual_candidate.name: equal-individual half mean pairwise squared within-individual distance
individual_candidate.minimum_support: k_i >= 2 valid captures; singleton within-individual spread is unresolved, not zero
individual_candidate.property: equals trace of unbiased sample covariance of observed locations

population_candidate.name: half mean pairwise squared distance among individual session centres
population_candidate.property: equals trace of unbiased sample covariance of individual centres
population_candidate.mechanical_null: under iid draws from an unchanged centre distribution, E[B] is invariant to sampled individual count m

mechanical_metric_preference.common_scale: W and B are squared-distance variance quantities; matched transformations are required for slope comparison
mechanical_metric_preference.centroid_uncertainty: must be handled prospectively by support rule, frozen de-noising sensitivity, or model-based abandonment of coordinate route before any density slopes are opened
mechanical_metric_preference.primary_abundance_boundary: N describes the session population, not the number of individuals eligible for W
